frame.description: A frame Handle to fill, such as ``frame_7f3a9c2e``.

output.description: The model-ready frame Handle and what was done to each column. ``result.get(name)`` finds one column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

frame.description: The new frame Handle, such as ``frame_5b6c7d8e``. It lacks hard-excluded and ``dropped`` columns other than Drop Candidates, has the indicator columns as Soft Exclusions later phases skip, and inherits the source frame's declarations.

source_frame.description: The frame Handle filled. It stays as it was, excluded columns included.

rows.description: Rows of the new frame: as many as the source frame.

columns.description: Every column the imputer was fitted on: those that fill or drop first, then ``passthrough``, each group in dataset order. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `strategy`, `missing`, `filled`, `fill_value`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: What ``impute`` did to one column. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name. A ``<column>_missing`` row is the indicator an ``mnar`` column adds.
Position 1, `strategy`: The column's strategy. A ``dropped`` column is not in the new frame, unless it is a Drop Candidate: see ``drop_candidates``.
Position 2, `missing`: Cells missing in the source frame, sentinels included; 0 for an indicator.
Position 3, `filled`: Cells the strategy filled. ``missing - filled`` cells are still missing: those of an ``mnar`` or ``passthrough`` column, and any a model left. 0 for a ``dropped`` column.

Position 4, `fill_value`: The one value a ``mean``, ``median``, ``mode``, ``constant`` or ``mnar`` column fills with. An ``mnar`` column keeps its nulls: its fill is on record here, not applied. Null for every other strategy. A Literal Field.
The columns routing marked ``dropped`` because profiling flagged them ``missingness.drop_candidate``.

columns.description: The Drop Candidates, in dataset order. They stay in the new frame with their missing values. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest.

dial.description: The profiling threshold that flagged them. Raise it to flag fewer.

operation.description: The Operation that takes the dial.

dial.description: The dial's argument path, such as ``thresholds.missingness.high_null_ratio``.

source.description: ``default`` when the library default decided, ``argument`` when the caller set it.

drop_candidates.description: Columns the library would drop, kept in the new frame: every drop is the Agent's own. To drop them, pass them to ``route`` as ``exclude_columns`` and build the imputer again from there. Null when there are none.
